The Pension Code allows you to elect among qualifying annuity formulas, and the figure shown for the retirement estimate is the larger option on your numbers. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The estimate for retiring now is based on age 56, 21.5 years of service, a highest average annual salary of $69,956.40, and 44 months before age 60. The Code permits an annuity beginning at age 55 or later, with a 0.25% reduction for each month the annuity begins before age 60, subject to the stated service exceptions. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The age-60 election under subsection (f-1) is not the formula used for the earlier retirement estimates because that election requires the annuity to begin no earlier than age 60. The age-and-service annuity under Section 11-130 applies, but the Pension Code text does not contain the conversion factors needed to put a figure on it. The provisions concerning withdrawal before age 55 do not apply here. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The comparison of future dates is a projection that holds the salary basis at today's level and assumes continuous employment to the stated retirement age.

Tax and insurance treatment are outside the Pension Code; the IRS and your fund or employer determine those matters.
